A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–I are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original sampling experiments and ablations on synthetic distributions, alanine dipeptide and biochemical sequence tasks, including Tables 1–4 and 6–9.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results on synthetic distributions, alanine dipeptide and biochemical sequence tasks, including Tables 1–4 and 6–9.

M1.justification: The SMC behaviour policy, importance-weighted replay, TB/SubTB training, chunk-based loss and adaptive tempering remain unchanged. The new overview diagram and revised explanations describe the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic targets under gradient-free and gradient-based conditions, alanine dipeptide conformations, and QM9, sEH, TFbind8 and L14-RNA1 sequence tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main benchmarks, buffer and loss ablations, molecular experiments and sequence-design comparisons. Newly cited SMC research is not added to the evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 5 and Appendices F, H and I retain the evaluation metrics, sample counts, training budgets, model sizes and hyperparameters. Both use 2,000 samples for the synthetic evaluation metrics and report end-of-training moving averages.

E4.justification: The flow, buffer-prioritisation, loss, tempering-threshold, subtrajectory-length and replay-ratio analyses are retained. The intermediate-target visualization moves from v1 Appendix G.2 to v2 Section 4.3 without adding an experiment.

E5.justification: Five-run means, standard deviations and error-bar reporting remain unchanged. However, v1 Appendix G.2 explicitly identifies the intermediate-target visualization as using the first seed; this disclosure is omitted when it becomes v2 Figure 2.

E6.justification: The numerical results and comparator entries in Tables 1–4 and 6–9 match exactly. The retained empirical image panels and sensitivity curves also match; the expanded discussion interprets existing evidence.

T1.justification: The mathematical framework, assumptions, losses, weighting formulas and appendix derivations are retained. Trajectory notation changes and the relocation of the partial-energy formula from v1 Equation 26 to v2 Equation 22 do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same unification, off-policy training, importance-weighted replay and empirical contributions. The rewritten conclusion emphasises the unifying framework already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds an explanation connecting corner-mode suppression under interpolation to the initial Gaussian density and explaining the benefit of learned corrections. It also qualifies the variance-based explanation of instability as 'likely'. The principal limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract, absent from v1. The implementation details and hyperparameters in the appendices are retained; the partial-energy parameterisation is relocated and explained more clearly.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.3 positions the framework against optimised SMC, including Guarniero et al. (2017), Heng et al. (2020) and Syed et al. (2024). Appendix A.2 adds four references on inference-time diffusion sampling. These extend the existing positioning without replacing it.

P1.justification: Focused rewrites affect experience replay, the conclusion and partial-energy explanations, with notation cleanup and an added impact statement. Most prose and section order remain intact. The displayed author name Nikolay Malkin changes to Esmeralda S. Whitammer.

P2.justification: The document adopts ICML typography and layout throughout and substantially reflows the appendices. v2 adds the training schematic in Figure 1, moves v1 Figure 5 into main-text Figure 2 while removing its initial-Gaussian panel, and regroups the appendix sensitivity plots.

improvement.justification: The new training schematic, clearer explanations, expanded optimised-SMC discussion and code-access information improve accessibility and research context. These limited gains outweigh the small loss of first-seed disclosure for the relocated visualization. The empirical and mathematical support remain unchanged.
